{{nihongo|'''Itate Shrine'''|伊達神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kii Province]].

[[File:Itate-jinja (Wakayama) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Torii}}]]
'''Date Shrine'' (Itate Jinja/Date Jinja) is located in {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|Q131314|qid=Q131314}}{{ill|Wakayama (city)|Q200747|qid=Q200747}} Sonobe. It is {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}), and {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old shrine rank}} is {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.Another name is "Sonobe Shrine (Sonobe Shrine)". Also {{ill|Shima Shrine|Q17212913|qid=Q17212913}} (Wakayama City{{ill|Nakanoshima|Q17226981|qid=Q17226981|lt=Nakanoshima}}), {{ill|Shizuhi Shrine|Q28693031|qid=Q28693031}} (Wada, Wakayama City, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamayama Shrine}}Setsusha), it is called ``Kinosanshoshya'' {{Sfn|Date Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=437-438}}.

== Enshrined God ==
The enshrined deities are as follows.<ref group="Note">The description of the two enshrined deities is according to the shrine history book [http://wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp/jdb/sys/user/GetWjtTbl.php?JinjyaNo=1012 Date Shrine] (Wakayama Prefecture Shrine Agency). However, in the "Meiji Shrine Journal", in addition to the two pillars, {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|Q11059454|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishimahime no Mikoto}} is listed as the Aiden deity. </ref>.
:* '''{{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|Q10881556|qid=Q10881556|lt=Goju Takekami}}''' (Itakeru no Mikoto) - {{ill|Mikogami|Q352176|qid=Q352176}} of {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Suenakison}}. The original deity.
:* '''{{ill|Kamuyaimimi|Q11588756|qid=Q11588756}}''' (Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto) - Later enshrined.In order to know the character of the "Itate deity" worshiped at Date Shrine, "{{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|Q11498726|qid=Q11498726}}" describes {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Empress Jingu}} is said to have enshrined ``Itayo no Kami'' in front of his ship when crossing to Korea {{Sfn|Date Shrine (Gods)|1986|p=320-321}}. Furthermore, in ``{{ill|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|Q11381815|qid=Q11381815}}'', Funatama Shrine, a Sumiyoshi Taisha Sessha, is said to be the deity of the Ki clan and the headquarters of ``Shima-kami, Shizuka-kami, and Date-kami'' {{Sfn|Date Shrine (Gods)|1986|p=320-321}}. In this way, ``Itate-kami'' has a deep relationship with ships, and is said to be the god of the Ki clan who traveled to various places by ship {{Sfn|Date Shrine (Gods)|1986|p=320-321}}. The personal deity Gojutake no Mikoto is a tree god symbolizing the ``Land of Trees'' (Ki Province), and since ships are made by cutting down trees, he was also considered the guardian deity of ships {{Sfn|Date Shrine (Gods)|1986|p=320-321}}.In addition, since Gojutake no Mikoto is the same deity as the enshrined deity {{ill|Itakiso shrine|ja|伊太祁曽神社|zh|伊太祁曾神社|qid=Q11379271}}, Date Shrine was also called ``Ichinomiya Daimyojin'' {{Sfn|Date Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1987|p=89}}. One theory is that in ``{{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|Q11604964|qid=Q11604964}}'', ``Kisansho Shrine'' is said to enshrine the three deities of Idakeso (Itake no Mikoto, Oya Tsuhime no Mikoto, and Tomato Hime no Mikoto) {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=362}}<ref group="Note">However, the two pillars other than Isotake no Mikoto are highly questionable {{Harv|Date Shrine (Gods)|1986|p=320-321}}. </ref>.

The enshrined deity, Yaimimi no Mikoto, is said to be the ancestor of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sonobe clan}}, who lived in this area in the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}}, according to the ``Illustrated Guide to Famous Places of Kii Province'' {{Sfn|Date Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=437-438}}. As mentioned later, the transfer to Sonobe was {{ill|Jōan (era)|Q1194188|qid=Q1194188|lt=Jōan}} 4 ({{ill|1174|Q19690|qid=Q19690}}), and based on this theory, it is believed that Kami Yaimimi no Mikoto was enshrined after the transfer.{{Sfn|Date Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=437-438}}

In addition to the two above-mentioned pillars, it is said that the father god of the 50 Takenomi no Mikoto, Suenmeison, was once enshrined as Gion {{ill|Gozu Tennō|Q11570247|qid=Q11570247}}{{Sfn|Date Shrine (Gods)|1986|p=320-321}}.

== History ==
[[File:Itate-jinja (Wakayama) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|main hall}}]]

== Founding ==
Founding date is unknown.

{{jalink|Cheng'an (Japan)|Q1194188|According to an ancient document dated 4 years ago ({{ill|1174|Q19690|qid=Q19690}}), "Kisansho Shrine" including Date Shrine Since it appears to have been located near the shrine|Q888184|Naemiya}}, the transfer to its current location in Sonobe is said to have taken place after that time {{Sfn|Date Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=437-438}}.

== Outline ==
In national history, both are known as Shima-kami and Shizuka-kami.{{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} In 11 years ({{ill|844|Q23835|qid=Q23835}}), he was given the lower rank of Seigoi, and in {{ill|Kashō|Q1373157|qid=Q1373157}}3 years ({{ill|850|Q30364|qid=Q30364}}) he was given the rank of junior fourth rank and lower. (Japan)|Q1075635|Jōgan}} In the 1st year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), he was promoted to Seishiyo (lower rank), in the 17th year of Jogan ({{jalink|875|Q23816}) }) Contains an article about the promotion of Junior Third Rank {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}}{{Sfn|Date Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=437-438}}.

In "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmōcho}}, {{ill|Kii Province|Q864053|qid=Q864053}}{{ill|Nagusa district|Q11415547|qid=Q11415547}} is ``Date Shrine'' In addition to being listed as ``Meishin-dai'' and listed in {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}, in ``{{ill|Kii no Kuni Jinmyō-chō|Q17210008|qid=Q17210008}}'' it is listed as ``Shoichii Date Okami'' {{Sfn|Date Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=437-438}}.Also, Date Shrine is {{ill|Shima Shrine|Q17212913|qid=Q17212913}} (Wakayama City {{ill|Nakanoshima|Q17226981|qid=Q17226981|lt=Nakanoshima}}) and {{ill|Shizuhi Shrine|Q28693031|qid=Q28693031}} (Wada, Wakayama City), it is said to have been called ``Kinosanshoshya'' {{Sfn|Date Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=437-438}}. The description of "Kisansho-sha" starts with the storage rice book of {{ill|Eishō (Heian period)|Q1193549|qid=Q1193549}}3 ({{ill|1048|Q19359|qid=Q19359}}), and also in "{{ill|Chūyūki|Q11363231|qid=Q11363231}}" {{ill|Tennin (era)|Q1193599|qid=Q1193599}}2nd year ({{ill|1109|Q19515|qid=Q19515}}) article, ``{{ill|Ryōjin Hishō|Q3010584|qid=Q3010584}}'' appears to be a Shiku divine poem {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=362}}. In "{{ill|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|Q11381815|qid=Q11381815}}", about the origin of Kisansho Shrine, {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sankan Conquest}} is said to have been enshrined to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668}}{{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=362}}.Our company has been compared to the above-mentioned ``Date Shrine,'' but according to ``{{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|Q11604964|qid=Q11604964}},'' there was a debate over this categorization in the {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}{{Sfn|Date Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=437-438}}. In other words, even though our company had previously called itself Date Shrine, during the {{ill|Kanpō|Q1145798|qid=Q1145798}} years ({{ill|1741|Q7573|qid=Q7573}}-{{ill|1744|Q7583|qid=Q7583}}) {{ill|Minato-Fukiage Shrine|Q11549496|qid=Q11549496}} in Ono-cho, Yama City claimed to be Shikinai Date Shrine, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Wakayama Domain}} recognized this claim {{Sfn|Date Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=437-438}}. Therefore, in "Ki Meisho Zue", Fukiage Shrine is compared to Date Shrine, and we called it "Sonobe Shrine" {{Sfn|Date Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=437-438}}.

Also, in "Zoku Fudoki", it is said that our shrine was burnt down by {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}}, but the truth is unclear {{Sfn|Date Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=437-438}}.

Entered {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} and changed the company name back to its old name, ``Date Shrine.'' In the 14th year of the Meiji era ({{ill|1881|ab|1881|af|1881|als|1881|am|1881 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1881|ar|1881|ary|1881|arz|1881|ast|1881|avk|1881|az|1881|azb|۱۸۸۱ (میلادی)|ba|1881 йыл|ban|1881|bar|1881|bat_smg|1881|bcl|1881|be|1881|be_x_old|1881|bg|1881|bn|১৮৮১|bpy|মারি ১৮৮১|br|1881|bs|1881.|ca|1881|cdo|1881 nièng|ce|1881 шо|ceb|1881|ckb|١٨٨١|crh|1881|cs|1881|csb|1881|cv|1881|cy|1881|da|1881|de|1881|diq|1881|el|1881|eml|1881|eo|1881|es|1881|et|1881|eu|1881|fa|۱۸۸۱|fi|1881|fiu_vro|1881|fo|1881|fr|1881|frp|1881|frr|1881|fur|1881|fy|1881|ga|1881|gan|1881年|gcr|1881|gd|1881|gl|1881|gn|1881|gv|1881|hak|1881-ngièn|he|1881|hi|१८८१|hif|1881|hr|1881.|hsb|1881|ht|1881 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1881|hy|1881|hyw|1881 թուական|ia|1881|id|1881|ilo|1881|io|1881|is|1881|it|1881|ja|1881年|jv|1881|ka|1881|kaa|1881|kk|1881 жыл|kn|೧೮೮೧|ko|1881년|krc|1881 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1881|ku|1881|kv|1881-ӧд во|la|1881|lb|1881|lez|1881 йис|li|1881|lij|1881|lld|1881|lmo|1881|lt|1881 m.|lv|1881. gads|mai|१८८१|map_bms|1881|mdf|1881|mg|1881|mhr|1881|mi|1881|min|1881|mk|1881|ml|1881|mr|इ.स. १८८१|mrj|1881 и|ms|1881|my|၁၈၈၁|myv|1881 ие|mzn|۱۸۸۱|nah|1881|nap|1881|nds|1881|nds_nl|1881|new|ई सं १८८१|nl|1881|nn|1881|no|1881|nrm|1881|nso|1881|oc|1881|olo|1881|or|୧୮୮୧|os|1881-æм аз|pa|1881|pap|1881|pl|1881|pnb|1881|pt|1881|qu|1881|ro|1881|ru|1881 год|rue|1881|sa|१८८१|sah|1881|sc|1881|scn|1881|sd|1881ع|se|1881|sh|1881.|shn|1881|si|1881|simple|1881|sk|1881|sl|1881|smn|1881|sq|1881|sr|1881|stq|1881|su|1881|sv|1881|sw|1881|szl|1881|ta|1881|te|1881|tet|1881|tg|Соли 1881|th|พ.ศ. 2424|tk|1881|tl|1881|tly|1881|tr|1881|tt|1881 ел|udm|1881 ар|uk|1881|ur|1881ء|uz|1881|vec|1881|vi|1881|vls|1881|vo|1881|wa|1881|war|1881|wuu|1881年|xmf|1881|yi|1881|za|1881 nienz|zea|1881|zh|1881年|zh_classical|一八八一年|zh_min_nan|1881 nî|zh_yue|1881年|qid=Q7808}}), it was ranked as {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}} in {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine rank system}}.

== God level ==
* Records of {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} dedication in the history of the Six Kingdoms
** {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jowa}} November 3, 11 years ({{ill|844|Q23835|qid=Q23835}}), from Jugoinoge to Shogoikege ('{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|cs|Šoku Nihonkóki|de|Shoku Nihon Kōki|es|Shoku Nihon Kōki|ff|Shoku Nihon Kōki|fr|Shoku nihon kōki|ja|続日本後紀|ko|속일본후기|pt|Shoku Nihon Kōki|zh|續日本後紀|qid=Q1041301}}') - Written as 'Date God'.
** October 21, 3rd year of {{ill|Kashō|Q1373157|qid=Q1373157}} ({{ill|850|Q30364|qid=Q30364}}), Junior Fourth Rank Lower (``{{ill|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Montoku Tennó Džicuroku|de|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|ff|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon Montoku tennō jitsuroku|ja|日本文徳天皇実録|ko|일본문덕천황실록|pt|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|zh|日本文德天皇實錄|qid=Q1052905}}'') - Written as ``Date God.''
** {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}} January 27th, 1st year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), from the lower rank of the fourth rank to the lower rank of the fourth rank (``{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}}'') - Written as ``Date God.''
** October 17, 17th year of the Jogan era ({{ill|875|Q23816|qid=Q23816}}), from the top of the fourth rank to the third rank of junior rank (``Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'') - Written as ``Date God.''
